PART XIV RETERMINATION OF IRON

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part XIV ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 August 1975, after the draft finalized by the Paper And its Products ( Excluding Packaging Materials ) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council, 0.2 This standard is mainly based on ISO/R 779-1968 ` Pulps - Determination of iron', issued by International Organization for Standardization.
0.3 Copper, iron and manganese, if present in pulp in more than traces, not It is, therefore, only discolour it but may also affect its dyeing properties. essential to know the quantities of each of these in the pulp. 0.4 In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960".

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard of iron in pulp. 2. QUALITY
( Part XIV ) prescribes the method for the determination

OF REAGENTS

2.1 Unless otherwise specified, pure chemicals and distilled water ( see IS : 1070-10607), freshly boiled and cooled, shall be employed in the tests. NOTE - ` Pure chemicals ' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities
which affect the results of test.

5.2 Spectrophotometer or Filter Colorimeter 6. CALIBRATION 6.1 Dilute the standard iron solution ten times so that 1 ml corresponds to 0'01 mg of iron. Pipette aliquots of 5'0, 10'0, 15'0 and 20'0 ml of the diluted solution into 50 ml volumetric flasks. Use the fifth flask for the preparation of a reference solution. Add to each flask 1 ml of hydroxylamine hydrochloride solution and 1 ml of orthophenanthroline hydrochloride solution and dilute to the mark with water. *After 15 minutes measure the optical density at 510 nm with the iron-free solution as a reference.
NOTE - Avoid exposure of the coloured solutions to direct sunlight. 6.2 The iron concentrations of the coloured solutions are 1'0, 2'0, 3'0 and 4'0 mg of iron per litre respectively. Plot on a graph the optical density values divided by the length of the cell, against the iron concentrations and check that the points lie on a straight line going through the origin,

8. PROCEDURE

8.1 Preparation of Test Sample - Weigh about IO g of pulp ( or 5 g for iron contents above 20 mg/kg) to the nearest 0'01 g. At the same time weigh out a separate sample for the determination of dry matter content.
4

IS : 6213 ( Part XIV) - 1975 8.2 Determination 8.2.1 Ash the test sample using a clean dish.
as described in IS : 6213 ( Part VII )-1971*

NOTE- Cleaning ofdishes: Wash the dish thoroughly; remove any spots in platinum dish by cleaning with fine sand. Boil the dish four times with dilute hydrochloric acid and avoid any possible contact with iron. Check in the following way that the dish is free from iron. Heat about 2 ml of the dilute hydrochloric acid diluted further with about IO ml of water in the dish. Allow to cool and add 1 ml of 1 ml of orthophenanthroline hydrochloride hydroxylamine hydrochloride solution, solution and 10 ml of sodium acetate solution. No red colour should appear. 8.2.2 In order to obtain a reagent blank, take another clean dish of the same type as used for the ashing of the test sample and treat as described To each dish add 5 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid and evaporate below. to dryness on a steam-bath. Repeat this once and then treat the residue with another portion of 2'5 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid and heat for 5 minutes on the steam-bath. Transfer the contents of the dishes to 50 ml To the insoluble residue in each volumetric flasks with the aid of water. dish add a further 2.5 ml of hydrochloric acid and warm on the steam-bath. Transfer this last portion to the main quantity in the volumetric flask with Add, in the following order, 1 ml of hydroxylamine the aid of water. hydrochloride solution, 1 ml of orthophenanthroline hydrochloride solution and, to obtain a pH value of 3 to 6, 15 ml of sodium acetate solution and If the solution is cloudy, filter through a dilute to the mark with water. glass filter or centrifug c. After 15 minutes measure the optical density at 510 nm with the reagent blank as a reference. Divide the reading by the length of the cell.

IS : 6213 ( Part XIV ) 1975 Report the result as the mean of the two determinations per kilogram ( parts per million ). in milligrams

NOTE-The precision of the method as such is high. Thus, the difference between results of duplicate tests is usually attributable to uneven distribution of the trace metal in the pulp.

10. TEST REPORT 10.1 The test report should state the results obtained and, moreover, indicate all the conditions of the test, any details of procedure regarded as optional or not laid down in this standard and any incidents that may have affected the results.
